# Pandamonium v1.0.76

This patch train upgrades the native Entertainment player: next-episode and autoplay, a jump-to-episode box, per-user favorites, and a continue-watching card. No backend, route, plugin-contract, dependency, schema, authentication, or stored-data change. Rollback remains signed v1.0.75 and the updater's retained pre-update snapshot.

## MAD-972 — Entertainment: player controls, favorites, and continue watching

### Problem

The native player stopped after every episode: there was no next-episode control and no autoplay. Long anime episode lists had to be paged through by hand, there was no way to save a favorite title, and nothing on the provider page showed what was being watched last.

### Implementation

The player bar gains a Next-episode button and an Autoplay toggle that advances on the video `ended` event. A Go-to-episode number box resolves a typed episode directly through the existing resolve contract instead of paging the list. Search results gain a favorite star, and the provider page renders a Continue-watching card plus the saved favorites. Autoplay, favorites, and the resume record persist per user in the existing `entertainment` preference, so no new endpoint or storage was added.

### Product value and UI visibility

A series keeps playing without manual clicks, any episode is one number away instead of hundreds of scrolls, and returning to a provider shows the last episode and saved titles. The new controls reuse the existing Entertainment surface classes, the red/black player palette, and inline monochrome SVG, matching the current player bar and result rows.

### Verification

Focused `tests/test_entertainment.py` passed 11 checks, including new source guards for the next/autoplay, jump, favorites, and resume controls. Three Chromium specs verify the settings/sidebar split and, in the new test, jump-to-episode, next-episode, the autoplay toggle, the continue-watching card, and favoriting a search result. The full Python suite passed 6,527 tests with five skips and the full Chromium suite passed all specs. Protected PR CI passed Python, browser, syntax, dependency, secret, workflow, container, and image gates.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No dependency, schema, environment variable, authentication, proxy contract, or stored-data change was introduced. Autoplay defaults to off; favorites and the resume record are additive per-user preferences under the existing `/api/prefs` store and fall back gracefully when unset. Next-episode advances within the loaded episode list and falls back to a numeric increment; providers remain governed by the installed AniCLI and PandaFlix packages.
